ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are two horizontal straight lines marked with the same arrow marks, indicating that they are parallel; a slanted straight line passes through these two parallel lines as a transversal. At the upper point of intersection, the angle labeled (3x−15)° is located below the upper horizontal line and on the left side of the transversal. At the lower point of intersection, the 105° angle is located below the lower horizontal line and on the left side of the transversal. Reasoning: These two angles are in the same relative position in the figure formed by two parallel lines and the same transversal, so they are corresponding angles. When parallel lines are cut by a transversal, corresponding angles are equal, therefore 3x−15=105. Solving gives 3x=120, so x=40.

method.method_draft: Read the figure as two parallel horizontal lines cut by a slanted transversal. Identify the angle labeled (3x−15)° at the upper intersection as being in the same relative position as the 105° angle at the lower intersection: both are below their respective parallel line and to the left of the transversal. Use the corresponding angles theorem to set 3x−15 = 105, then solve x = 40.
